title: Design → Code
outcome: The work under any item a person names from the plan becomes working code: it is designed against the project's standards, its evals are written before it is built, and it is built test first by a builder who never sees the tests. Defects are fixed test first too, quickly and without a full design.
why: Left alone, agents build from a guess and check their own work, so a pass proves nothing.
proof: The work is designed before it is coded, against the project's standards.
Every expected result has a test that was written and shown to fail before its code.
The builder never sees a test or an eval.
must_not: Tell the builder the steps, or show the builder the tests.

touches.title: Gather the work under a chosen plan item
Gather the whole tree under a chosen item
Collect each story's context from its guidance
Write the evals that check the work
Write the evals of the chosen work, with what must never happen, before it is built
Update the evals as the work changes
Add the steps an eval may use on a kind of surface
Keep the evals from the builder, and flag a build that read them
Design the work
Design the chosen work, how it is built and what its surface shows
Update the design as the work changes
Build the work test first
Write all the tests for the work, and show each one fails
Build the code until every test passes, then tidy it, without seeing the tests
Write the usage guide that tells the eval how to reach the built work
Update the tests and the code as the work changes
Fix defects test first
Understand the defect: its feature in the product model, its tests and why they pass, and its root cause
Write the tests that prove the defect, and show each one fails
Fix the code and run every test, then tidy it, without seeing the tests
/shape-eval writes the hidden eval
The build is given the business intent, never the eval
